plan: This is a single-round auction. The optimal bidding strategy in a second-price sealed-bid auction with rational bidders is to bid your true value. This is because bidding less than your value risks losing the auction when you could have won and made a profit. Bidding more than your value risks winning the auction but paying more than the item is worth to you, resulting in a loss. Therefore, I will bid my true value.

This is the first round, so I have no history to learn from. The optimal bidding strategy in a second-price sealed-bid auction, assuming rational bidders, is to bid slightly below your true value. Given my value of $17, I will bid a bit below that, say $16.9. This ensures I win if my value is higher than the others' bids, and I don't overpay.

This is a sealed-bid second-price auction. With rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below your true value. Since all bidders are rational and know each other are rational, bidding exactly your value is not optimal. I will bid slightly below my value, say 95% of my value, to account for the other bidders' rationality.
